## What

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Mamba Kernels` runs all 943 cases of `tests/kernels/mamba` in one pytest process and measures 36.6–48.7m wall (40.1m median) across 14 recent main builds. This replaces it with four content-named jobs — SSD Single Example, SSD Continuous Batch, Ops, and GDN — each running whole files or whole folders, so the timeline says what ran and every file's per-process setup is paid exactly once per lane. The `(MI250)` mirror splits the same way.

This is the third design iteration, each measured on a scoped build: case-level hash sharding ([90995](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90995)) failed both budgets — per-process kernel setup repeats per shard (summed pytest 67.0m vs 35.9m unsharded). Three file-level jobs ([91011](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91011)) fixed cost (+5.5 worker-minutes) and reconciled coverage exactly, but the single-file SSD job measured 22.8m pytest against the 20m target. This revision extracts that file's parametrized groups into two flat wrappers over a shared helper, splitting SSD into two ~11m units. Both validations are documented in the comments.

## Old

```
kernels-mamba-test   "(H200 MIG 35GB) Mamba Kernels"   35.9m pytest / 36.9m wall (build 90947)
└── pytest -v -s kernels/mamba        tests/kernels/mamba/  (17 test files + cpu/, flat)
mirror: amd-kernels-mamba-test   "(MI250) Mamba Kernels"   23.9m pytest / 25.4m wall
```

## New

```
tests/kernels/mamba/
├── ssd/
│   ├── _mamba_ssm_ssd.py                                   (new: shared helpers, never collected)
│   ├── single_example/test_mamba_ssm_ssd_single_example.py (test_mamba_chunk_scan_single_example, 48 cases)
│   └── cont_batch/test_mamba_ssm_ssd_cont_batch.py         (both continuous-batch tests, 46 cases)
├── gdn/        (new folder: 6 GDN test files, mirrors vllm/.../mamba/gdn/)
├── ops/        (new folder: 10 files, mirrors vllm/.../mamba/ops/)
├── cpu/        (unchanged, CPU lane)
└── utils.py    (unchanged helper, imported by absolute path)

kernels-mamba-ssd-single-example   "(H200 MIG 35GB) Mamba SSD Single Example"     pytest kernels/mamba/ssd/single_example
kernels-mamba-ssd-cont-batch       "(H200 MIG 35GB) Mamba SSD Continuous Batch"   pytest kernels/mamba/ssd/cont_batch
kernels-mamba-ops-test             "(H200 MIG 35GB) Mamba Ops Kernels"            pytest kernels/mamba/ops
kernels-mamba-gdn-test             "(H200 MIG 35GB) Mamba GDN Kernels"            pytest kernels/mamba/gdn
                                                                                  + find kernels/mamba -maxdepth 1 -name 'test_*.py' (root sweep)
each with its own mirror:  amd-<key>  "(MI250) Mamba ..."
```

Original file → wrappers: `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py::test_mamba_chunk_scan_single_example` → `ssd/single_example/test_mamba_ssm_ssd_single_example.py`; `::test_mamba_chunk_scan_cont_batch` and `::test_mamba_chunk_scan_cont_batch_prefill_chunking` → `ssd/cont_batch/test_mamba_ssm_ssd_cont_batch.py`; `segsum` / `ssd_minimal_discrete` / `generate_random_inputs` / `generate_continuous_batched_examples` → `ssd/_mamba_ssm_ssd.py`. Bodies are verbatim; a static diff confirms every non-import line is unchanged, and 48 + 42 + 4 = 94 matches the measured case count.

Old → new keys: `kernels-mamba-test` → the four keys above (union of their coverage equals the old job's; the retired key has no other consumers). The legacy optional `:amd: (MI300) Mamba Kernels` step in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` is a separately rendered pipeline, untouched — its whole-directory command still collects everything.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Predictions from measured per-function timings in the build 91011 SSD job log (single-example span 7.7m over a partial capture, ~11–12m with all 48 cases; cont-batch ~10–11m) and measured per-file timings from builds 90947/90995:

| job | pytest (est.) | running wall (est.) | non-pytest overhead (est.) | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Mamba SSD Single Example | ~11–12m | ~13.5m | ~1.5m | container setup |
| Mamba SSD Continuous Batch | ~10–11m | ~12.5m | ~1.5m | container setup |
| Mamba Ops Kernels | ~14.1m (measured, build 91011) | ~15.2m (measured) | ~1.1m | container setup |
| Mamba GDN Kernels | ~1.8m (measured) | ~2.9m (measured) | ~1.1m | container setup |
| MI250 SSD x2 / Ops / GDN | ~8m each / 6.6m / 1.5m | ~9.5m each / 8.3m / 3.3m | ~1.7m each | container setup |

- **Slowest job ~14.1m pytest (Ops, measured); SSD halves estimate to ~11–12m.** All well inside the 20m target.
- **Aggregate:** base lane ~44.6 worker-minutes vs 36.9 before (**~+7.7 vs the ≤20 budget**); mirror ~30.1 vs 25.4 (**~+4.7**). The increase over the v2 estimates is one more repeated container setup for the second SSD job.
- Coverage equivalence: moved files are `git mv` (path-prefix-only node ID changes); the SSD split is body-verbatim extraction (static diff-checked). Every previously-run case is under exactly one new command.

## Notes

- **Why not hash-shard:** measured, not hypothetical — per-file fleet-cold vs warm inflation (SSD 94 cases: ~18m → 33m across 3 shards; `test_memcpy_u64_tiled.py` 120 cases: 1.8m → 13.9m). Details in the first validation comment.
- **Grouping is by content, not duration:** `gdn/` and `ops/` mirror `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/{gdn,ops}`; the SSD wrappers split along the file's own test-function boundary (single-example vs continuous-batch), each in its own `ssd/` subdirectory so every job runs a directory. The GDN job's root sweep runs any test file added at the `kernels/mamba` root.
- **Other path updates:** `.buildkite/hardware_tests/cpu.yaml`, `run-cpu-test-arm.sh` and the `(B200) Kernels` job point at the moved `ops/` and `gdn/` files.
- The Ops job is now the slowest at a measured 14.1m; if it grows past target it hash-shards cleanly as a directory (`ops/` has 10 files, ~800 cases) without the per-file setup penalty this directory showed at case level — that was the failed experiment, noted only to explain why Ops stays one job today.

AI assistance: this change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code); I have reviewed every changed line. Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this job or `tests/kernels/mamba` CI wiring (checked open PRs for "mamba kernels" / "kernels-mamba"). Local verification: `yaml.safe_load` on both edited YAML files, `py_compile` + ruff check/format on the new and moved files, static body-equivalence diff for the SSD split, the test-tethering pre-commit check (`--all`, exit 0), and its unit tests (138 passed). GPU validation of this head to follow in the comments.

## Validation — build [90995](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90995) @ 99187ac (fails both budgets; rework planned)

Scoped build with `kernels-mamba-test` + `amd-kernels-mamba-test`. All 5 replicas passed, and coverage reconciles exactly against the unsharded baseline (908 = 301+308+299 passed on the base lane; 707 = 368+339 on the mirror). Checkout confirmed at the PR head on every replica. But the measurements falsify the PR's predictions:

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Base lane shard 1 | 21.4m | 22.6m | 1.2m | checkout + container setup |
| Base lane shard 2 | 22.4m | 24.0m | 1.6m | checkout + container setup |
| Base lane shard 3 | 23.2m | 24.5m | 1.3m | checkout + container setup |
| Mirror shard 1 | 20.2m | 21.7m | 1.5m | checkout + container setup |
| Mirror shard 2 | 21.3m | 23.2m | 1.9m | checkout + container setup |

**Runtime verdict: FAIL.** Slowest shard 23.2m pytest (predicted ~12m) vs the 20m target; the mirror's slowest is 21.3m.

**Cost verdict: FAIL on the base lane.** The shards sum to 67.0m pytest against a 35.9m unsharded baseline: 71.1 worker-minutes vs 36.9 before → **+34.2, over the ≤20 budget** (mirror: 44.9 vs 25.4 → +19.5, barely inside). I predicted "pytest total is unchanged" and that was wrong.

**Cause.** Hash-sharding by case scatters each file's cases across three pytest processes, and this directory has large per-process/per-file warm-up that the unsharded single process pays once. Measured per-file, warm (baseline) → fleet-cold (sum across the 3 shards):

| file | cases | warm | fleet-cold (3 shards) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py | 94 | ~17–19m | 33.0m |
| test_memcpy_u64_tiled.py | 120 | ~1.8m | 13.9m |
| test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py | 117 | ~3.1m | 6.0m |
| (all others) | ~600 | ~13m | ~13.5m |

So the inflation is not container overhead (stays ~1–2m per replica) — it is repeated kernel setup/compile and lost in-process cache reuse inside pytest. No shard count fixes this: at N=2 the slowest shard gets slower (~28m), at N=4 the aggregate cost roughly doubles again.

**Rework.** I'm converting this PR from case-level hash sharding to file-level named jobs, so every file's setup is paid exactly once per lane: the dominant `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` (~17–19m warm, under target as a singleton) becomes its own named job, and the remaining 13 files move into `gdn/` and `ops/` folders mirroring `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/{gdn,ops}` behind two more named jobs. Predicted aggregate stays within a few worker-minutes of the 36.9m baseline; a fresh validation build will follow on the new head.

## Validation 2 — build [91011](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91011) @ 006a16bd (named whole-unit jobs)

Scoped build with all six new keys. Every job passed on both lanes, on the rebased PR head. Coverage reconciles exactly against the unsharded `main` baseline (build 90947): base lane 908 = 94 + 796 + 18 passed; mirror 707 = 94 + 599 + 14. Nothing duplicated or dropped.

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Mamba SSD Kernels | 22.8m | 24.3m | 1.5m | container setup |
| Mamba Ops Kernels | 14.1m | 15.2m | 1.1m | container setup |
| Mamba GDN Kernels | 1.8m | 2.9m | 1.1m | container setup |
| MI250 SSD / Ops / GDN | 15.8m / 6.6m / 1.5m | 17.6m / 8.3m / 3.3m | ~1.7m each | container setup |

**Cost verdict: PASS, both lanes.** Base lane: 42.4 worker-minutes vs 36.9 before → **+5.5** (≤20 budget). Mirror: 29.2 vs 25.4 → **+3.8**. As predicted, per-file setup is paid once per lane now (summed pytest 38.6m ≈ the 35.9m baseline; the delta is normal run-to-run variance).

**Runtime verdict: FAIL on the SSD job (base lane).** Measured 22.8m pytest against the 20m target — the ~17–19m prediction was extrapolated from a partially-captured baseline span and this run came in slower; everything else is well under (Ops 14.1m, GDN 1.8m; all mirror jobs ≤15.8m).

**Adjustment.** Splitting `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` itself is the follow-up anticipated in the PR body: extract its parametrized groups into flat wrapper files over a shared helper so the SSD coverage can be divided into two whole units (per-case timings from build 90995 put a clean two-way split at ~11–12m pytest per half, and the mirror's 15.8m total means it can keep running the file whole). I will update this PR and re-validate the SSD jobs only.

## Validation 3 — build [91028](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91028) @ c3525833 (one extraction bug, fixed)

Six of eight jobs passed. **SSD Continuous Batch failed on both lanes**: my wrapper extraction dropped the `A` argument from one of the three `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` call sites in `test_mamba_chunk_scan_cont_batch_prefill_chunking` (4 cases errored with `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'chunk_size'` — the kernel binds positionally, so the missing `A` shifted everything). Transcription slip, not a design problem; my original static equivalence check compared line *sets* and missed it because `A,` also appears in a destructuring block — the re-check now counts line multiplicity and shows zero missing lines. Fixed in `75f6f92e`.

Measurements from the passing jobs (their inputs are untouched by the fix, so these stand):

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mamba SSD Single Example | 10.9m | 12.5m | 1.6m |
| Mamba SSD Continuous Batch (42/46 ran) | 11.0m | 13.0m | 2.0m |
| Mamba Ops Kernels | 13.3m | 15.4m | 2.1m |
| Mamba GDN Kernels | 2.0m | 3.3m | 1.3m |
| MI250 SSD Single Example | 8.0m | 9.6m | 1.6m |
| MI250 SSD Continuous Batch (42/46 ran) | 7.4m | 8.9m | 1.6m |
| MI250 Ops / GDN | 6.6m / 1.5m | 8.2m / 3.1m | ~1.6m |

The SSD split lands where predicted (~11m per half vs the 22.8m single-process measurement that forced it), and every measured job is comfortably inside the 20m target. The four prefill-chunking cases are small (sub-minute each in the unsharded baseline), so the fixed job projects to ~12–13m pytest. A final scoped build on the fixed head will re-run the Continuous Batch jobs and confirm 46/46.

## Validation 4 (final) — build [91048](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91048) @ 381dae11: all green, both budgets pass

Full 8-job scoped build on the fixed head. All jobs passed on both lanes, including the previously failing Continuous Batch jobs (46/46 on each). Coverage reconciles exactly against the unsharded `main` baseline (build 90947): base lane **908 = 48 + 46 + 796 + 18** passed; mirror **707 = 48 + 46 + 599 + 14**. Before triggering, the tree was verified against current `main`: all 15 moved files are byte-identical, the SSD split loses zero lines under a multiplicity-aware diff, and the test-function census is unchanged (77 non-SSD + 3 SSD).

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Mamba SSD Single Example | 10.9m | 12.1m | 1.1m | container setup |
| Mamba SSD Continuous Batch | 12.0m | 13.1m | 1.1m | container setup |
| Mamba Ops Kernels | 15.1m | 16.1m | 1.0m | container setup |
| Mamba GDN Kernels | 2.0m | 3.5m | 1.5m | container setup |
| MI250 SSD Single Example | 7.9m | 9.7m | 1.7m | container setup |
| MI250 SSD Continuous Batch | 8.3m | 9.8m | 1.5m | container setup |
| MI250 Ops / GDN | 7.0m / 1.4m | 8.4m / 3.1m | ~1.5m each | container setup |

**Runtime verdict: PASS.** Slowest job is Ops at 15.1m pytest (baseline unsharded job: 35.9m). Both SSD halves landed within a minute of their ~11–12m predictions; everything else matched the build-91011/91028 measurements.

**Cost verdict: PASS, both lanes.** Base lane: 44.7 worker-minutes vs 36.9 before → **+7.8** (≤20 budget). Mirror: 31.0 vs 25.4 → **+5.6**. Summed pytest 40.0m vs the 35.9m baseline — the delta is the three extra in-process collections/fixture passes; per-replica non-pytest overhead stayed ~1–1.7m as predicted.

**Prediction accuracy:** worst miss was the first SSD estimate (~17–19m predicted from a partially-captured baseline span vs 22.8m measured) — corrected by the two-way split; all v3/v4 predictions landed within ~1m. The earlier hash-shard failure and its per-file inflation data are in the first two validation comments.

- `(B200) Kernels Shard %N` (`kernels-b200`): the source dependency and the command now point at `tests/kernels/mamba/gdn/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+from einops import rearrange, repeat
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+# All kernels exercised here are pure Triton, so they run on any backend
+# that the vLLM platform layer treats as a CUDA-alike device or as XPU.
+DEVICE = current_platform.device_type
+
+# Added by the IBM Team, 2024
+
+# Adapted from https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/blob/v2.2.4/mamba_ssm/modules/ssd_minimal.py
+
+
+# this is the segsum implementation taken from above
+def segsum(x):
+    """Calculates segment sum."""
+    T = x.size(-1)
+    x = repeat(x, "... d -> ... d e", e=T)
+    mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(T, T, device=x.device, dtype=bool), diagonal=-1)
+    x = x.masked_fill(~mask, 0)
+    x_segsum = torch.cumsum(x, dim=-2)
+    mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(T, T, device=x.device, dtype=bool), diagonal=0)
+    x_segsum = x_segsum.masked_fill(~mask, -torch.inf)
+    return x_segsum
+
+
+def ssd_minimal_discrete(X, A, B, C, block_len, initial_states=None):
+    """Arguments:
+        X: (batch, length, n_heads, d_head)
+        A: (batch, length, n_heads)
+        B: (batch, length, n_heads, d_state)
+        C: (batch, length, n_heads, d_state)
+
+    Return:
+        Y: (batch, length, n_heads, d_head)
+
+    """
+    assert X.dtype == A.dtype == B.dtype == C.dtype
+    assert X.shape[1] % block_len == 0
+
+    # Rearrange into blocks/chunks
+    X, A, B, C = (
+        rearrange(x, "b (c l) ... -> b c l ...", l=block_len) for x in (X, A, B, C)
+    )
+
+    A = rearrange(A, "b c l h -> b h c l")
+    A_cumsum = torch.cumsum(A, dim=-1)
+
+    # 1. Compute the output for each intra-chunk (diagonal blocks)
+    L = torch.exp(segsum(A))
+    Y_diag = torch.einsum("bclhn,bcshn,bhcls,bcshp->bclhp", C, B, L, X)
+
+    # 2. Compute the state for each intra-chunk
+    # (right term of low-rank factorization of off-diagonal blocks; B terms)
+    decay_states = torch.exp(A_cumsum[:, :, :, -1:] - A_cumsum)
+    states = torch.einsum("bclhn,bhcl,bclhp->bchpn", B, decay_states, X)
+
+    # 3. Compute the inter-chunk SSM recurrence; produces correct SSM states at
+    #    chunk boundaries
+    # (middle term of factorization of off-diag blocks; A terms)
+    if initial_states is None:
+        initial_states = torch.zeros_like(states[:, :1])
+    states = torch.cat([initial_states, states], dim=1)
+    decay_chunk = torch.exp(segsum(F.pad(A_cumsum[:, :, :, -1], (1, 0))))
+    new_states = torch.einsum("bhzc,bchpn->bzhpn", decay_chunk, states)
+    states, final_state = new_states[:, :-1], new_states[:, -1]
+
+    # 4. Compute state -> output conversion per chunk
+    # (left term of low-rank factorization of off-diagonal blocks; C terms)
+    state_decay_out = torch.exp(A_cumsum)
+    Y_off = torch.einsum("bclhn,bchpn,bhcl->bclhp", C, states, state_decay_out)
+
+    # Add output of intra-chunk and inter-chunk terms
+    # (diagonal and off-diagonal blocks)
+    Y = rearrange(Y_diag + Y_off, "b c l h p -> b (c l) h p")
+    return Y, final_state
+
+
+def generate_random_inputs(batch_size, seqlen, n_heads, d_head, itype, device=DEVICE):
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    A = -torch.exp(torch.rand(n_heads, dtype=itype, device=device))
+    dt = F.softplus(
+        torch.randn(batch_size, seqlen, n_heads, dtype=itype, device=device) - 4
+    )
+    X = torch.randn((batch_size, seqlen, n_heads, d_head), dtype=itype, device=device)
+    B = torch.randn((batch_size, seqlen, n_heads, d_head), dtype=itype, device=device)
+    C = torch.randn((batch_size, seqlen, n_heads, d_head), dtype=itype, device=device)
+
+    return A, dt, X, B, C
+
+
+def generate_continuous_batched_examples(
+    example_lens_by_batch,
+    num_examples,
+    full_length,
+    last_taken,
+    exhausted,
+    n_heads,
+    d_head,
+    itype,
+    device=DEVICE,
+    return_naive_ref=True,
+):
+    # this function generates a random examples of certain length
+    # and then cut according to "example_lens_by_batch" and feed
+    # them in continuous batches to the kernels.
+    # If if return_naive_ref=True, the naive torch implementation
+    # ssd_minimal_discrete will be used to compute and return
+    # reference output.
+
+    # generate the full-length example
+    A, dt, X, B, C = generate_random_inputs(
+        num_examples, full_length, n_heads, d_head, itype
+    )
+
+    if return_naive_ref:
+        Y_min, final_state_min = ssd_minimal_discrete(
+            X * dt.unsqueeze(-1), A * dt, B, C, block_len=full_length // 4
+        )
+
+    # internal function that outputs a cont batch of examples
+    # given a tuple of lengths for each example in the batch
+    # e.g., example_lens=(8, 4) means take 8 samples from first eg,
+    #       4 examples from second eg, etc
+    def get_continuous_batch(example_lens: tuple[int, ...]):
+        indices = []
+        for i, x in enumerate(example_lens):
+            c = last_taken.get(i, 0)
+            indices.append((c, c + x))
+            last_taken[i] = (c + x) % full_length
+            exhausted[i] = last_taken[i] == 0
+
+        return (
+            torch.concat([x[i, s:e] for i, (s, e) in enumerate(indices)]).unsqueeze(0)
+            for x in (dt, X, B, C)
+        )
+
+    # internal function that maps "n" to the appropriate right boundary
+    # value when forming continuous batches from examples of length given
+    # by "full_length".
+    # - e.g., when n > full_length, returns n % full_length
+    #         when n == full_length, returns full_length
+    def end_boundary(n: int):
+        return n - ((n - 1) // full_length) * full_length
+
+    IND_E = None
+    for spec in example_lens_by_batch:
+        # get the (maybe partial) example seen in this cont batch
+        dt2, X2, B2, C2 = get_continuous_batch(spec)
+
+        # get the metadata
+        cu_seqlens = torch.tensor((0,) + spec, device=device).cumsum(dim=0)
+        seq_idx = torch.zeros(
+            cu_seqlens[-1], dtype=torch.int32, device=cu_seqlens.device
+        )
+        for i, (srt, end) in enumerate(
+            zip(
+                cu_seqlens,
+                cu_seqlens[1:],
+            )
+        ):
+            seq_idx[srt:end] = i
+
+        # for cont batch
+        if IND_E is None:
+            IND_S = [0 for _ in range(len(spec))]
+        else:
+            IND_S = [x % full_length for x in IND_E]
+        IND_E = [end_boundary(x + y) for x, y in zip(IND_S, spec)]
+
+        # varlen has implicit batch=1
+        dt2 = dt2.squeeze(0)
+        X2 = X2.squeeze(0)
+        B2 = B2.squeeze(0)
+        C2 = C2.squeeze(0)
+        yield (
+            [Y_min[s, IND_S[s] : IND_E[s]] for s in range(num_examples)]
+            if return_naive_ref
+            else None,
+            cu_seqlens,
+            seq_idx,
+            (A, dt2, X2, B2, C2),
+        )

+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.kernels.mamba.ssd._mamba_ssm_ssd import (
+    DEVICE,
+    generate_random_inputs,
+    ssd_minimal_discrete,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.ssd_combined import (
+    mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mamba2_attn import compute_varlen_chunk_metadata
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_cuda_alike() or current_platform.is_xpu()),
+    reason="Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels require a CUDA-alike or XPU device.",
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("itype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n_heads", [4, 16, 32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d_head", [5, 8, 32, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_len_chunk_size", [(112, 16), (128, 32)])
+def test_mamba_chunk_scan_single_example(d_head, n_heads, seq_len_chunk_size, itype):
+    # this tests the kernels on a single example (bs=1)
+
+    # TODO: the bfloat16 case requires higher thresholds. To be investigated
+
+    if itype == torch.bfloat16:
+        atol, rtol = 5e-2, 5e-2
+    else:
+        atol, rtol = 8e-3, 5e-3
+
+    # set seed
+    batch_size = 1  # batch_size
+    # ssd_minimal_discrete requires chunk_size divide seqlen
+    # - this is only required for generating the reference seqs,
+    #   it is not an operational limitation.
+    seqlen, chunk_size = seq_len_chunk_size
+
+    A, dt, X, B, C = generate_random_inputs(batch_size, seqlen, n_heads, d_head, itype)
+
+    Y_min, final_state_min = ssd_minimal_discrete(
+        X * dt.unsqueeze(-1), A * dt, B, C, chunk_size
+    )
+
+    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor((0, seqlen), device=DEVICE).cumsum(dim=0)
+    cu_chunk_seqlens, last_chunk_indices, seq_idx_chunks = (
+        compute_varlen_chunk_metadata(cu_seqlens, chunk_size)
+    )
+    # varlen has implicit batch=1
+    X = X.squeeze(0)
+    dt = dt.squeeze(0)
+    A = A.squeeze(0)
+    B = B.squeeze(0)
+    C = C.squeeze(0)
+    Y = torch.empty_like(X)
+    final_state = mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen(
+        X,
+        dt,
+        A,
+        B,
+        C,
+        chunk_size,
+        cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens.to(torch.int32),
+        cu_chunk_seqlens=cu_chunk_seqlens,
+        last_chunk_indices=last_chunk_indices,
+        seq_idx=seq_idx_chunks,
+        out=Y,
+        D=None,
+    )
+
+    # just test the last in sequence
+    torch.testing.assert_close(Y[-1], Y_min[0, -1], atol=atol, rtol=rtol)
+
+    # just test the last head
+    # NOTE, in the kernel we always cast states to fp32
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        final_state[:, -1].to(torch.float32),
+        final_state_min[:, -1].to(torch.float32),
+        atol=atol,
+        rtol=rtol,
+    )

## Validation — build [90995](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90995) @ 99187ac (fails both budgets; rework planned)

Scoped build with `kernels-mamba-test` + `amd-kernels-mamba-test`. All 5 replicas passed, and coverage reconciles exactly against the unsharded baseline (908 = 301+308+299 passed on the base lane; 707 = 368+339 on the mirror). Checkout confirmed at the PR head on every replica. But the measurements falsify the PR's predictions:

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Base lane shard 1 | 21.4m | 22.6m | 1.2m | checkout + container setup |
| Base lane shard 2 | 22.4m | 24.0m | 1.6m | checkout + container setup |
| Base lane shard 3 | 23.2m | 24.5m | 1.3m | checkout + container setup |
| Mirror shard 1 | 20.2m | 21.7m | 1.5m | checkout + container setup |
| Mirror shard 2 | 21.3m | 23.2m | 1.9m | checkout + container setup |

**Runtime verdict: FAIL.** Slowest shard 23.2m pytest (predicted ~12m) vs the 20m target; the mirror's slowest is 21.3m.

**Cost verdict: FAIL on the base lane.** The shards sum to 67.0m pytest against a 35.9m unsharded baseline: 71.1 worker-minutes vs 36.9 before → **+34.2, over the ≤20 budget** (mirror: 44.9 vs 25.4 → +19.5, barely inside). I predicted "pytest total is unchanged" and that was wrong.

**Cause.** Hash-sharding by case scatters each file's cases across three pytest processes, and this directory has large per-process/per-file warm-up that the unsharded single process pays once. Measured per-file, warm (baseline) → fleet-cold (sum across the 3 shards):

| file | cases | warm | fleet-cold (3 shards) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py | 94 | ~17–19m | 33.0m |
| test_memcpy_u64_tiled.py | 120 | ~1.8m | 13.9m |
| test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py | 117 | ~3.1m | 6.0m |
| (all others) | ~600 | ~13m | ~13.5m |

So the inflation is not container overhead (stays ~1–2m per replica) — it is repeated kernel setup/compile and lost in-process cache reuse inside pytest. No shard count fixes this: at N=2 the slowest shard gets slower (~28m), at N=4 the aggregate cost roughly doubles again.

**Rework.** I'm converting this PR from case-level hash sharding to file-level named jobs, so every file's setup is paid exactly once per lane: the dominant `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` (~17–19m warm, under target as a singleton) becomes its own named job, and the remaining 13 files move into `gdn/` and `ops/` folders mirroring `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/{gdn,ops}` behind two more named jobs. Predicted aggregate stays within a few worker-minutes of the 36.9m baseline; a fresh validation build will follow on the new head.

## Validation 2 — build [91011](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91011) @ 006a16bd (named whole-unit jobs)

Scoped build with all six new keys. Every job passed on both lanes, on the rebased PR head. Coverage reconciles exactly against the unsharded `main` baseline (build 90947): base lane 908 = 94 + 796 + 18 passed; mirror 707 = 94 + 599 + 14. Nothing duplicated or dropped.

| job | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Mamba SSD Kernels | 22.8m | 24.3m | 1.5m | container setup |
| Mamba Ops Kernels | 14.1m | 15.2m | 1.1m | container setup |
| Mamba GDN Kernels | 1.8m | 2.9m | 1.1m | container setup |
| MI250 SSD / Ops / GDN | 15.8m / 6.6m / 1.5m | 17.6m / 8.3m / 3.3m | ~1.7m each | container setup |

**Cost verdict: PASS, both lanes.** Base lane: 42.4 worker-minutes vs 36.9 before → **+5.5** (≤20 budget). Mirror: 29.2 vs 25.4 → **+3.8**. As predicted, per-file setup is paid once per lane now (summed pytest 38.6m ≈ the 35.9m baseline; the delta is normal run-to-run variance).

**Runtime verdict: FAIL on the SSD job (base lane).** Measured 22.8m pytest against the 20m target — the ~17–19m prediction was extrapolated from a partially-captured baseline span and this run came in slower; everything else is well under (Ops 14.1m, GDN 1.8m; all mirror jobs ≤15.8m).

**Adjustment.** Splitting `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` itself is the follow-up anticipated in the PR body: extract its parametrized groups into flat wrapper files over a shared helper so the SSD coverage can be divided into two whole units (per-case timings from build 90995 put a clean two-way split at ~11–12m pytest per half, and the mirror's 15.8m total means it can keep running the file whole). I will update this PR and re-validate the SSD jobs only.

## Validation 3 — build [91028](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91028) @ c3525833 (one extraction bug, fixed)

Six of eight jobs passed. **SSD Continuous Batch failed on both lanes**: my wrapper extraction dropped the `A` argument from one of the three `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` call sites in `test_mamba_chunk_scan_cont_batch_prefill_chunking` (4 cases errored with `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'chunk_size'` — the kernel binds positionally, so the missing `A` shifted everything).
